newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin had five bypasses - U.S. surgeon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin had five bypasses - U.S. surgeon.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation on Tuesday involved five bypasses but this should not affect his chances of a full recovery, a U.S. cardiac surgeon who was present said.

Professor George Noon told Reuters by telephone: "It is not unusual to see five bypasses. The important thing is that the vessels that were diseased were all able to be bypassed and he (Yeltsin) has done very well."
Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin on Tuesday declined to spell out how many bypasses he had performed, saying he did not have Yeltsin's consent to reveal the exact figure.
Noon, from the Bailey Medical Centre in Houston, came to Moscow with Professor Michael DeBakey as a consultant to the Russian team that carried out the operation on Yeltsin.

"It was very standard and everything went in a very routine manner without complications," he said. "The vessels that were diseased were bypassed and it ended up with the number five," Noon said, adding that a couple of Yeltsin's arteries had sections which were completely blocked.

However the high number of bypasses would make no difference to the speed of recovery now that the blood supply to the heart had been reestablished. "He (Yeltsin) has really responded well and is doing fine." He said there were no other special areas of concern after the operation and "a routine convalescence is what we are looking for."
